testFuzz_AdjustmentsStayWithinTheImmutab.details: They are additive and non-negative: MIN is unreachable from above, MAX is clamped.

test_ARaisedCapStillFills().details: The end-to-end check that the cap is a ceiling and not a required value: the market's      fee is zero on the fork, and a non-zero cap must still let a seller through.

test_BlueSupplyRateIsRealAndSane().details: The floor is worth nothing if the number behind it is a stub. This measures it on the      fork, against the same USDC/WETH market the idle sleeve actually sits in.

test_FloorAboveTheHardMaxStopsTheQuote().details: The alternative would be to clamp at MAX_RATE_BPS and keep buying below the floor —      exactly the value destruction the floor forbids. Refusing to quote is the only honest      answer. Blue paying 35% does not happen on the fork, hence the mock.

test_PolicyWithoutVaultRefusesToQuote().details: Failing closed matters here: an unskewed, unfloored quote is precisely the static bid      this whole mechanism replaces, and a half-finished deployment must not produce one.

test_RatificationGasWithTheDynamicPolicy.details: `isRatified` now reads Blue's rate model on top of the vault's own book. The bound is      deliberately loose — it is an alarm for a change that made ratification expensive, not      a performance target. What would be unacceptable is a seller giving up on the take.

test_SkewMovesTheBidAsTheBookFills().details: This is the whole point of the skew. The cap is still there and still binds, but the      approach to it is now priced: each lot is bought a little cheaper than the last, so      concentration is paid for by the seller who causes it rather than worn by depositors.

test_SkewSaturatesWhenHeldExceedsTheCap(.details: Reachable in one move: the owner lowers `maxUnits` under a book already built.

test_StaleBidIsRefusedOnceTheSkewHasMove.details: The offer sitting in the Mempool is a struct with a fixed tick; nothing cancels it. What      protects the vault is that `isRatified` re-reads the policy at the instant of the take,      and the policy has moved. Without the skew this could only happen when the owner changed      the rate; with it, the vault's own fills disarm its stale offers.

test_TheBidPromisesNoContinuousFeeByDefa.details: Midnight's continuous fee is set by its governance, at any time, and applies to offers      already broadcast. Every Base market prices it at zero today; the point of the default      is that the day it stops being zero, Plumb's takes revert instead of quietly handing      the depositors' yield over.

test_TheCapIsBoundedByWhatMidnightWouldA.details: Pinned against the upstream constant rather than restated: Midnight's      `ConstantsLib.MAX_CONTINUOUS_FEE` is `uint32(uint256(0.01e18) / uint256(365 days))`,      enforced in `setMarketContinuousFee` and `setDefaultContinuousFee`. Anything above it      is a number the owner could write and no market could ever match — a policy that reads      like a decision without being one.

test_TheShippedAdjustmentsNeverReachTheC.details: If `rateBps + volSpreadBps + skewBps` reached `MAX_RATE_BPS`, a full book would quote      the same rate as a half-full one and the skew would stop saying anything. The shipped      set tops out at 17.5%, well inside the 30% clamp.

test_TheShippedMarginLeavesTwentyEightPo.details: `effectiveRateBps` reverts with `BelowBlueFloor` when `blueRate + margin` exceeds      `MAX_RATE_BPS`: Plumb refuses to bid rather than quote above the bound that protects      the counterparty. Correct, and the reason the pair (margin, Blue rate) has to be      checked as a pair — a margin chosen on its own merits can silently pin the vault      offline the day Blue spikes.      The bound is arithmetic and exact: the bid survives every Blue rate up to      `MAX_RATE_BPS - margin`. At the shipped margin of 200 bps that is **28%** — Blue's USDC      supply rate reads 4.6% at the pinned block and its stress peaks are an order of      magnitude below 28%. What this test pins is the headroom, so that raising the margin      later is a choice made against a number.

test_VolSpreadPricesCollateralRisk().details: The spread is flat and configured, not inferred — but it is applied by the same      on-chain path as the rest, so the bot cannot quote around it.

failed().notice: Returns true if any test assertion has failed.

targetSenders().notice: Returns sender allowlist configured via `targetSender` (empty means no sender allowlist).

testFuzz_AdjustmentsStayWithinTheImmutab.notice: The adjustments can never breach the immutable bounds.

test_ARaisedCapStillFills().notice: A fee Plumb has priced in does not block the take.

test_BlueSupplyRateIsRealAndSane().notice: The vault reads a real, non-zero supply rate from the live Blue market.

test_EnabledMarketNeedsANonZeroCap().notice: An enabled market with no cap cannot be priced, so it cannot be configured.

test_FloorAboveTheHardMaxStopsTheQuote().notice: When Blue out-earns anything Plumb may legitimately bid, Plumb stops quoting.

test_FloorDoesNotTouchARateAlreadyAboveI.notice: Above the floor, the floor is inert — it is a floor, not a peg.

test_FloorLiftsARateThatWouldDestroyValu.notice: Below the floor, Plumb demands the floor — it never buys under its own idle yield.

test_OnlyOwnerSetsVaultAndMargin().notice: Only the owner moves the policy's own wiring.

test_OwnerCannotConfigureAnUnboundedAdju.notice: A rate configured above the adjustment bounds is refused outright.

test_PolicyWithoutVaultRefusesToQuote().notice: Without its vault, the policy refuses to quote rather than quoting unadjusted.

test_RatificationGasWithTheDynamicPolicy.notice: The floor puts an IRM call on the critical path of every take. Measure it.

test_RatificationRefusesAnOfferPromising.notice: And ratification enforces it: the bot cannot promise more than the policy accepts.

test_SkewMovesTheBidAsTheBookFills().notice: The bid steps back as the market fills, instead of holding still then refusing.

test_SkewSaturatesWhenHeldExceedsTheCap(.notice: Held units above the cap saturate the skew rather than overshooting it.

test_StaleBidIsRefusedOnceTheSkewHasMove.notice: A bid broadcast before the book filled stops being takeable on its own.

test_TheBidPromisesNoContinuousFeeByDefa.notice: Plumb starts out refusing to pay any continuous fee at all.

test_TheCapIsBoundedByWhatMidnightWouldA.notice: The cap cannot be set beyond the fee Midnight would itself accept.

test_TheOwnerCanPriceInAContinuousFee().notice: Raising the cap is the owner's call, and it moves the bid.

test_TheShippedAdjustmentsNeverReachTheC.notice: And the three adjustments together never saturate the clamp on their own.

test_TheShippedMarginLeavesTwentyEightPo.notice: The margin we ship leaves room for a Blue rate far above anything USDC has printed.

test_VolSpreadPricesCollateralRisk().notice: Two markets, two collateral risks, two prices.
